title: Athena connector config
description: The OPAQUE `config:` block for mac.connector.athena (record §5.3). MAC never reads a key inside it. NOTHING HERE HAS A DEFAULT VALUE: a region, a workgroup or a catalog default would be one deployment's setting compiled into the instrument that serves every deployment -- which is the defect data_plane.profile_table already records against itself ('it used to fall back to a literal workgroup name -- one ontology's Athena workgroup, compiled into the tooling that serves every ontology, and reached by any bundle whose own config was missing').

region.description: The region handle the Athena and Glue clients are built for. A handle the deployment supplies; this file ships no default.

workgroup.description: The Athena workgroup handle. Required, and deliberately without a default: a workgroup belongs to the ontology being served, not to the SDK serving it.

catalog.description: The Athena data catalog handle to set as the query execution context.

database.description: The default database for the query execution context. Optional: a fully-qualified relation reference does not need one.

output.description: The result output location. May be null ONLY when the workgroup enforces a managed output location -- a fact of the account, not of this file, which is why validate_config reports its absence rather than resolving it (§6.3's honest limit: a rule JSON Schema cannot express belongs to validate_config).

glue_databases.description: Role -> database handle, e.g. the fact and dimension databases a harvest enumerates.

allow_ddl.description: Permit the ONE write verb, create_or_replace_view. Defaults to FALSE and belongs only in the out-of-band deployment overlay: §4.5 requires that a published, shipped bundle can never be used to write.

account.description: PRESENT ONLY TO FORBID A VALUE. The account id is derived at runtime via STS and is never shipped; typing it as null makes a leaked account id a SCHEMA failure at the mount tier rather than a finding some later gate might or might not run.
